primary_sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual — Transaction Isolation Levels
claims: InnoDB supports READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, and SERIALIZABLE, with REPEATABLE READ as the default.

Under REPEATABLE READ, consistent reads in one transaction use the snapshot established by the first consistent read; unique-index unique searches lock the found record while other search conditions can use gap or next-key locks.

Under READ COMMITTED, each consistent read gets a fresh snapshot and locking reads/UPDATE/DELETE normally lock records rather than gaps except for foreign-key and duplicate-key checks, so phantom-row problems may occur.
READ UNCOMMITTED permits dirty reads, while SERIALIZABLE is stricter and converts plain SELECT to SELECT ... FOR SHARE when autocommit is disabled.

primary_sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual — Consistent Nonlocking Reads
claims: InnoDB consistent reads use multiversioning to present a point-in-time snapshot without setting locks on the accessed records.
REPEATABLE READ reuses the first consistent-read snapshot within a transaction, whereas READ COMMITTED uses a fresh snapshot for each consistent read.

primary_sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual — SET TRANSACTION Statement
claims: Transaction isolation can be configured at global, session, or next-transaction scope, and the default isolation level is REPEATABLE READ.

A session-level change applies to subsequent transactions in that session and does not retroactively change the current transaction; a global change affects subsequent sessions rather than existing sessions.
